web_evidence.title: Arch of Triumph | Penguin Random House Higher Education
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained Chapter 1 excerpt narrates Ravic and the woman externally as he and she while separately marking Ravic's thoughts, establishing third-person narration throughout the opening.

web_evidence.title: Writing Techniques in Arch of Triumph
web_evidence.note: This Gale-derived study-guide section explicitly states that the novel uses third-person point of view focused on Ravic and Joan and discusses that technique through the ending.

search_log: Searched "Arch of Triumph" "Erich Maria Remarque" with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, narrator, third person, and narrative-perspective terms.
Opened the Penguin Random House edition page and inspected its sustained authorized Chapter 1 excerpt.
Opened the BookRags/Gale writing-techniques page, which explicitly identifies third-person point of view across the novel.
Opened EBSCO Research and the Erich Maria Remarque Peace Center pages; their plot summaries verified the work and Ravic's centrality but summary grammar was not treated as person evidence.

A University of Stirling thesis search result described the novel as combining third-person perspective with a close portrayal of Ravic, but the PDF returned HTTP 403 when opened and was excluded from web evidence.
Google Books and Internet Archive targeted searches did not yield an additional accessible sustained interior excerpt.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and narrates Ravic in third person, often with close access to his thoughts. Goodreads event passages repeatedly show this structure, especially the externally marked thought passages and the sustained he-centered narration in q00369 and q00374. First-person language in q00363 and q00366 is explicitly embedded as Ravic's direct thought, while first and second person elsewhere occur in dialogue or generic maxims. The authorized publisher opening independently confirms sustained third-person narration, and the Gale-derived technique description explicitly extends that classification to the novel as a whole. No evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found; the main scope limitation is that the authorized prose excerpt covers only the opening.
